chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Haytham al-Sayrafi and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A single loan [earns a reward] of eighteen [times], and if he dies, it will be counted as Zakat.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for giving a loan to a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the immense spiritual merit of lending to a believer, equating a single loan to eighteenfold reward, a multiplier reflecting the virtue of relieving financial distress. Notably, this reward is preserved and counted toward the lender's Zakat even after death, underscoring the continuity of charitable deeds in the Shia understanding of posthumous spiritual accounting.
